title: Zipf's Law: The Strange Order Hiding in Everything
question: Why do wildly different systems — language, cities, earthquakes, the internet — all obey the same hidden mathematical pattern?
summary: From the frequency of English words to the size of cities, an astonishing number of unrelated systems follow the same simple rule: the second-most-common thing is about half as common as the most common, the third about a third, and so on.
